answer: Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed temporal half-life, so an identity must provide sustained, verifiable honest service to retain influence; brief activity cannot bank durable trust. In the EigenTrust matrix, a freshly spawned Sybil with no endorsements from established peers has near-zero eigenvector centrality, and reciprocal, transitive weighting limits fabricated links from amplifying it. Thus it cannot meet consensus thresholds merely by multiplying identities, even when clustered like an island in a lagoon or layered like shale.
